Long-term fundamental strength is evident as profit grew 50% over five years while the price grew only 6%, indicating fundamentals are outpacing the stock and creating a potentially undervalued situation [E55]. Mishka Exim Ltd carries significant valuation risk because its core profitability has collapsed sharply in the most recent quarter, with the quarterly operating margin plunging to 2% in Jun 2026 from 9% in the year-ago quarter, representing a severe six percentage point drop [E31]. This sudden deterioration in operational performance makes the trailing P/E of 33.2x highly vulnerable and potentially detached from current reality [E1]. Compounding this multiple risk, the company trades at an EV/EBITDA of 23.54x, which is more than triple the sector benchmark of 7.48x, signaling that the market is paying an aggressive premium for earnings that are currently under severe pressure [E11]. Furthermore, investors receive no cash return for taking on these operational and valuation risks, as the dividend yield sits at a barren 0.00% [E4]. Conceded: the company maintains a positive operating margin expansion of two percentage points over a three-year period in the TTM data [E30] and offers a modest margin of safety against its DCF value [E45].

The trailing P/E of 33.2x sits below the sector benchmark of 35.78x [E1, E6], and the price-to-book ratio of 2.69x trades at a clear discount to the sector benchmark of 3.77x [E7]. While EV/EBITDA is elevated [E11], fundamentals have outpaced the stock over a five-year period with profit growing 50% against a price increase of only 6% [E55]. Conceded: TTM operating margin rose by two percentage points over three years to reach 9% [E30], and profits grew 50% against a 6% price increase over five years [E55]. However, the bull's reliance on sector P/E and P/B benchmarks [E6, E7] masks a glaring valuation disconnect in the EV/EBITDA multiple, which stands at 23.54x compared to a sector benchmark of just 7.48x [E11]. Furthermore, pointing to multi-year trends or DCF outputs [E44, E46] completely glosses over the catastrophic collapse in quarterly operating margins to 2% in Jun 2026 from 9% in the year-ago quarter [E31], rendering historical averages and forward models dangerously obsolete. The total absence of any dividend yield [E4] further strips away any margin of safety for shareholders while the company struggles with this acute margin compression.
